title: notifications: a push device's stored locale is never read, but the schema says pushes to it render in that locale
body:
domain:server#4 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbacSXJQqAztgt4UMrS

Filing gate: ① an out-of-scope finding of the #29041 dev, escalated by the contract review of PR #29794 (record 6596752211, ③ out-of-scope 1 and 3, ④ 4). Filed by `domain:server` seat 4. ⛔ Not a claim. Suggested-grade: p3 (a description that promises behaviour the tree does not have; no wrong delivery).

## What happens

`UserDeviceSchema.locale` (`packages/spec/src/system/push-device.zod.ts`) says "Device locale … that pushes to this device are rendered in", and the `sys_user_device.locale` field (`packages/services/service-messaging/src/objects/user-device.object.ts`) says the same. The registry stores it (`device-registry.ts` writes `request.locale`, reads it back onto the device), but nothing renders by it:

- `push-channel.ts` sends the notification's own `title` and `body`, which the dispatcher already rendered in the **recipient's** language (`sys_user.locale`, then the deployment default; `dispatcher.ts`, `digest-render.ts`).
- There is no push template: `TEMPLATE_CHANNELS` (`objects/notification-template.object.ts`) is `email` and `sms`, so a `(topic, push, locale)` row cannot exist.

So a user whose phone is set to `ja-JP` and whose account is `en` gets English pushes, while the contract says Japanese. Source reading on PR #29794's head `3aac0c59`.

## Wanted

Pick one, and say which in the PR:

1. **Make the text true to the tree (smallest).** Both descriptions say the column is stored for a later per-device rendering and that pushes render in the recipient's language today. Spec description change only.
2. **Make the tree true to the text.** Add `push` to `TEMPLATE_CHANNELS` with a per-topic push template (title and body, length-capped as the channel caps them), and render per device locale, falling back to the recipient locale. This is a widening and needs its own declaration first.

Either way, pin it: a test that sends to a device whose locale differs from the user's and asserts which language arrives.

Serial: after PR #29794 (same files).

Dedupe: searched `push locale`, `push template`, `service-push`; nearest are #29041 (the channel) and #29768 (device origin). **New.**

Links back: #29041, PR #29794, #29768, #13881.
